title: Dedicated queue pressure triage and long-term mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the week of 2026-02-15 we observed repeated sustained queue pressure on several Dedicated GPU pools serving PL customer traffic. The immediate symptoms were elevated request latency, request queuing inside the serving runtime, and partial SLA degradation for customers on reserved capacity. This ticket captures the triage timeline, short-term mitigations we executed, root-cause hypotheses, validation experiments, and required postmortem action items to prevent recurrence and guarantee throughput under common workload patterns.

Observed impact and scope:
- Affected pools: eu-west-1-prod-dedicated-gpu-{a,b,c} (3 pools) for customers with reserved capacity.
- Duration: 2026-02-15 08:10 UTC -> 2026-02-16 03:00 UTC (primary incident window) with recurrent smaller spikes through 2026-02-23.
- User-visible: median p95 latency increased by ~2.3x; increased token cost due to retries for some SDK clients.
- Root-cause candidate: combination of an autoscaler change (recently shipped policy adjustment to reduce scale-up aggressiveness) plus a KV cache eviction pattern that increased per-request GPU work for mid-length sequences.

Triage timeline and key events:
- 2026-02-15 08:15 UTC: Oncall alerted by SLO alert for dedicated-pool-p95-latency.
- 2026-02-15 08:30 UTC: SRE opened temporary additional capacity (burst pool) and routed 15% of traffic to fallback compatible model variants (lower-cost quantized variants) to reduce pressure.
- 2026-02-15 09:00 UTC: Initial hypothesis documented: autoscaler down-scaling threshold and slower scale-up windows allowed queues to build when several large requests arrived simultaneously.
- 2026-02-15 11:30 UTC: Deployed a hotfix to reduce scale-up cooldown from 120s -> 60s for affected pools (canary -> all).
- 2026-02-15 14:00 UTC: Observed partial recovery, but repeated spikes returned due to large KV cache churn from a customer A/B test generating long-tail sequence prefixes.
- 2026-02-16 00:45 UTC: Rolled back a recently deployed runtime change to aggressive KV cache trimming (PR #4821) and validated request time reduced by ~18%.
- 2026-02-16 03:00 UTC: Incident marked mitigated; monitoring continued through 2026-02-23.

Investigation findings and evidence:
- Autoscaling behavior: The autoscaler commit (commit 9c3b4f) lowered target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds to improve cost-efficiency, increasing the time to reach the prior steady-state instance count under burst load. Metrics: horizontal-pool-scaling.log shows scale-up latency increased by median 45s post-change.
- KV cache behavior: Runtime telemetry shows increased eviction rate on mid-sized sequences (512-1024 tokens) after a config change intended to reduce memory footprint. This increased decoding per-request by ~12% and reduced batching effectiveness.
- Workload characteristics: One customer ran an A/B experiment that temporarily increased burstiness (many concurrent long-sequence requests), which exposed the regression.
- Correlation: The worst latency windows correlate with simultaneous occurrence of the autoscaler change + KV cache trimming + customer burst.

Short-term mitigations executed:
- Burst augmentation: provisioned two temporary burst pools and applied traffic steering to take 20% of requests off the impacted pools (runbook step executed by SRE).
- Scale-up cooldown change: reduced cooldown from 120s to 60s to improve responsiveness during bursts (rolled back in 48h after validation plan).
- Runtime config rollback: reverted KV cache trimming (PR #4821) and re-deployed prior cache config to restore batching efficiency.
- Customer communication: Notified affected customers via account manager and provided post-incident summary draft.

Long-term action items (see action_items for owners/due dates):
- Revise autoscaling policy to make scale-up adaptive to request queue growth (not only utilization thresholds).
- Add a synthetic load test that mixes long-tail sequence distributions to surface KV cache eviction regressions in CI.
- Improve runtime telemetry: expose per-pool batching efficiency and KV hit/miss ratios to Console dashboards.
- Create per-customer burst detection & soft-throttling guidance for Dedicated customers to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Update runbooks to include a clear checklist for temporary augmentation and rollback criteria.

Acceptance criteria:
- New autoscaler behavior validated in staging against synthetic burst test with p95 latency within SLA for 100% of runs.
- CI has a new test that fails on KV cache regression (deterministic reproduction) and linked to PR gating.
- Console dashboard tile created showing batching-utilization and KV hit rate for each dedicated pool.

Links and artifacts:
- Runbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/incident-runbook
- Incident dashboard (grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/dedicated-pool-incident-2026-02
- Hotfix PR for cooldown: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892
- KV cache rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4830
- Postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/ENG-12567-dedicated-queue-pressure.md

Notes and trade-offs discussed:
- Trade-off: Keeping cooler autoscaler thresholds saved ~$Xk/month but increased blast radius for sudden bursts. Decision: prioritize predictable throughput for Dedicated customers; revert cost-driven threshold change for Dedicated pools and investigate more nuanced cost controls.
- Trade-off: More aggressive KV caching increases memory pressure per instance; we will evaluate quantization and per-model cache sizing instead of global trimming.
- Follow-on: Investigate a hybrid routing policy that detects queue growth and momentarily routes requests to compatible fallback variants without manual augmentation.

2026-02-20 09:30 UTC — Aisha Patel: Postmortem draft created and linked. Added reproduction notes and initial synthetic scenario for CI. Requested review from runtime and autoscaler owners (Gina Lee, Mateo Ruiz).

2026-02-25 16:45 UTC — Gina Lee: Performed load test with synthetic long-tail sequences in staging. Reproduced KV eviction regression locally; proposed adding KV hit/miss histogram to telemetry (see PR #4924).

2026-03-02 11:20 UTC — Mateo Ruiz: Proposed autoscaler change: introduce queue-length trigger and two-step scale-up (fast then steady). Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/202
2026-03-08 14:05 UTC — Security Review (J. Park): No sensitive data exposure from added telemetry. Approval to proceed with dashboarding and CI tests.
2026-03-10 10:50 UTC — Luca Moretti: Ready for design review on runbook changes and for scheduling a canary of the autoscaler change in the next cycle (2026-W11).
